2022-11-30-chatgpt.title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT as a public research preview
2022-11-30-chatgpt.whatChanged: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free research preview. People could talk to a language model in plain conversation and ask follow-up questions.
2022-11-30-chatgpt.whyCare: Chat became the way most people first used a language model.
2022-11-30-chatgpt.before: People used language models mainly through research demos, APIs and specialist tools.
2022-11-30-chatgpt.after: Anyone with a browser could use a capable model through a chat window.
2022-11-30-chatgpt.learn: Treat chat as one interface among several. Keep the conversation layer separate from the model and the business logic behind it.
2022-11-30-chatgpt.architectureImplication: Design the chat interface, the model and the business workflow as separate layers, so each can change on its own.

2023-03-14-gpt4.title: OpenAI releases GPT-4, which accepts both images and text
2023-03-14-gpt4.whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-4, a large multimodal model that accepts image and text input. It improved on professional and academic benchmarks.
2023-03-14-gpt4.whyCare: Harder knowledge work and image-plus-text use cases became realistic, and so did the need for evaluation and controls.
2023-03-14-gpt4.before: Most GenAI applications ran on weaker, text-only models.
2023-03-14-gpt4.after: Teams could build for more complex reasoning, higher-stakes workflows and image-plus-text input.
2023-03-14-gpt4.learn: Test the model on your own tasks before you raise the stakes. Add evaluation and controls as capability grows.
2023-03-14-gpt4.architectureImplication: A stronger model still needs evaluations, good data, controls and workflow design around it.

2023-06-13-function-calling.title: OpenAI adds function calling so models can return structured tool calls
2023-06-13-function-calling.whatChanged: OpenAI added function calling to its API. A model can pick a described function and return structured arguments that code can use to call an API or tool.
2023-06-13-function-calling.whyCare: Applications could let models trigger software actions reliably.
2023-06-13-function-calling.before: Developers parsed free text or relied on fragile prompt conventions to connect models to software.
2023-06-13-function-calling.after: Models return structured tool calls that code can validate and run.
2023-06-13-function-calling.learn: Let the model choose the action and let your code run it. Check arguments and permissions before any tool runs.
2023-06-13-function-calling.architectureImplication: Separate model judgment from deterministic execution. Put validation and permission checks between them.

2024-02-15-gemini15-context.title: Google previews Gemini 1.5 Pro with a one-million-token context window
2024-02-15-gemini15-context.whatChanged: Google introduced Gemini 1.5 Pro with a standard 128,000-token context window. A one-million-token window was available in private preview for selected developers and enterprise customers.
2024-02-15-gemini15-context.whyCare: Very long context changed the choice between retrieval and putting source material straight into the prompt.
2024-02-15-gemini15-context.before: Teams split large document sets into small chunks and retrieved a few at a time.
2024-02-15-gemini15-context.after: Some workloads could send far larger collections directly. Retrieval still mattered for cost, freshness, permissions and precision.
2024-02-15-gemini15-context.learn: Test long context, retrieval and a mix of both on your data. Compare cost, latency and accuracy.
2024-02-15-gemini15-context.architectureImplication: Choose between long context, retrieval or both based on data size, freshness, latency, cost and access control.

2024-05-13-gpt4o.title: OpenAI releases GPT-4o, one model for text, vision and audio
2024-05-13-gpt4o.whatChanged: OpenAI introduced GPT-4o, trained as a single model across text, vision and audio. It can respond to audio input in as little as 232 milliseconds.
2024-05-13-gpt4o.whyCare: Voice and multimodal products need fewer separate speech, vision and language components.
2024-05-13-gpt4o.before: Voice applications chained several models and conversion steps.
2024-05-13-gpt4o.after: One model can handle more of the interaction directly.
2024-05-13-gpt4o.learn: For voice and multimodal products, plan for streaming, interruptions, session state and cost.
2024-05-13-gpt4o.architectureImplication: Design multimodal systems around streaming, latency, session state and interruption handling.

2024-07-23-llama31.title: Meta releases Llama 3.1, including an openly available 405B model
2024-07-23-llama31.whatChanged: Meta released Llama 3.1, including a 405B model with a 128K context window. The weights are available for broad use under Meta's license.
2024-07-23-llama31.whyCare: Teams could run a model close to the frontier on infrastructure they control.
2024-07-23-llama31.before: Frontier-level capability sat mostly behind closed, hosted APIs.
2024-07-23-llama31.after: Enterprises had a strong open-weight option for control, customization and deployment.
2024-07-23-llama31.learn: Compare licensing, data location, hosting cost and the skills you need to run it before you self-host.
2024-07-23-llama31.architectureImplication: Include deployment control, licensing and operating effort in model selection, next to quality and price.

2024-09-12-o1.title: OpenAI releases o1, a model that reasons before it answers
2024-09-12-o1.whatChanged: OpenAI released o1-preview, a model series that spends more time reasoning before responding. It improves on harder science, coding and math tasks.
2024-09-12-o1.whyCare: Reasoning time became a setting you choose, with a trade-off between quality, latency and cost.
2024-09-12-o1.before: Teams treated most model calls as the same kind of single-pass answer.
2024-09-12-o1.after: Teams can choose when a task is worth more reasoning time and cost.
2024-09-12-o1.learn: Route tasks by difficulty and value. Save expensive reasoning for the tasks that need it.
2024-09-12-o1.architectureImplication: Add routing between fast and reasoning models, based on task difficulty, risk and cost.

2024-10-22-computer-use.title: Anthropic releases computer use, letting Claude operate graphical software
2024-10-22-computer-use.whatChanged: Anthropic released computer use in public beta. Claude can look at screenshots, move a pointer, click and type through software interfaces.
2024-10-22-computer-use.whyCare: Agents can act in systems that have no API, though reliability and security remain hard.
2024-10-22-computer-use.before: Automation needed APIs, scripts or fragile browser automation.
2024-10-22-computer-use.after: A model can operate existing graphical software in a general way.
2024-10-22-computer-use.learn: Run computer-use agents in a sandbox. Limit credentials and plan how to check and undo their actions.
2024-10-22-computer-use.architectureImplication: Computer use widens what agents can reach. Add sandboxing, credential limits, verification and recovery.

2024-11-25-mcp.title: Anthropic open-sources MCP, a standard for connecting AI to tools and data
2024-11-25-mcp.whatChanged: Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol, a standard way to connect AI assistants to data sources, business tools and development environments.
2024-11-25-mcp.whyCare: Teams can build a connector once and use it with many AI clients.
2024-11-25-mcp.before: Each application or framework needed its own connection to each tool and data source.
2024-11-25-mcp.after: Tools and data sources can expose one interface that many AI clients use.
2024-11-25-mcp.learn: Check which of your tools already offer MCP servers. Adopt a protocol once the ecosystem around it grows.
2024-11-25-mcp.architectureImplication: Use a shared protocol for tool and data connections to reduce coupling between AI clients and systems.

2025-01-20-deepseek-r1.title: DeepSeek releases R1, an open-weight reasoning model with low API prices
2025-01-20-deepseek-r1.whatChanged: DeepSeek released R1 and smaller distilled reasoning models with open weights under the MIT license. API prices were $0.14 to $0.55 per million input tokens and $2.19 per million output tokens.
2025-01-20-deepseek-r1.whyCare: Reasoning became available at lower cost and with open weights, which put pressure on closed-model prices.
2025-01-20-deepseek-r1.before: Advanced reasoning came mainly from a few closed providers.
2025-01-20-deepseek-r1.after: Teams had more choice across quality, hosting control, openness and cost.
2025-01-20-deepseek-r1.learn: Keep your design portable across providers. Test new models quickly when capability and prices move.
2025-01-20-deepseek-r1.architectureImplication: Avoid tying the architecture to one provider. Model routing and portability gain value as prices change.

2025-03-11-responses-agents.title: OpenAI launches the Responses API, built-in tools and an Agents SDK
2025-03-11-responses-agents.whatChanged: OpenAI released the Responses API, built-in tools for web search, file search and computer use, and an Agents SDK with tracing.
2025-03-11-responses-agents.whyCare: Teams could buy core agent infrastructure as a managed service and write less orchestration code.
2025-03-11-responses-agents.before: Teams assembled tool use, orchestration, tracing and state with custom code or separate frameworks.
2025-03-11-responses-agents.after: More of the agent harness comes from the platform.
2025-03-11-responses-agents.learn: Decide which parts of the agent harness to buy and which to build. Check what you can export or move later.
2025-03-11-responses-agents.architectureImplication: Managed agent runtimes change build-versus-buy decisions. Weigh speed of delivery against portability.

2025-04-09-a2a.title: Google announces A2A, a protocol for agents to work with other agents
2025-04-09-a2a.whatChanged: Google announced the Agent2Agent protocol so agents from different vendors and frameworks can communicate and coordinate.
2025-04-09-a2a.whyCare: Agent-to-agent interoperability became a stated industry goal. Standards still need adoption before teams can rely on them.
2025-04-09-a2a.before: Multi-agent systems assumed one framework, one vendor or custom conventions.
2025-04-09-a2a.after: A shared protocol could reduce coupling between agent systems as adoption grows.
2025-04-09-a2a.learn: Track which vendors support A2A. Adopt it when your partners or customers need cross-vendor agents.
2025-04-09-a2a.architectureImplication: Plan agent boundaries so a standard protocol can replace custom connections later.

2025-05-21-managed-mcp-background.title: OpenAI adds remote MCP servers and background mode to the Responses API
2025-05-21-managed-mcp-background.whatChanged: OpenAI added support for remote MCP servers, a background mode for long-running tasks, and further reliability and privacy features to its Responses API.
2025-05-21-managed-mcp-background.whyCare: Managed runtimes now handle more of the connections and long-running execution that agents need.
2025-05-21-managed-mcp-background.before: Teams built connectivity and long-running execution for agents themselves.
2025-05-21-managed-mcp-background.after: The platform covers more of the operational agent harness.
2025-05-21-managed-mcp-background.learn: Compare managed convenience with portability, visibility, security needs and lock-in.
2025-05-21-managed-mcp-background.architectureImplication: Managed runtimes can absorb connectivity and long-running work. Keep observability and an exit path in your design.

2026-09-01-enterprise-evals.title: Teams start to evaluate the path an agent takes as well as its answer
2026-09-01-enterprise-evals.whatChanged: Teams now need to check which tools an agent used, which path it took and whether it stayed inside policy. Checking the final answer alone misses these.
2026-09-01-enterprise-evals.whyCare: A correct-looking answer can come from an unsafe path. This matters once agents take actions.
2026-09-01-enterprise-evals.before: Teams evaluated whether the final answer was correct.
2026-09-01-enterprise-evals.after: Teams evaluate the result and the sequence of actions that produced it.
2026-09-01-enterprise-evals.learn: Add trajectory checks to your evaluations. Keep audit logs and use human review for risky actions.
2026-09-01-enterprise-evals.architectureImplication: Combine output evaluations, trajectory evaluations, audit logs, policy checks and risk-based human review.

2026-05-19-gemini-spark.title: Google announces Gemini Spark, a persistent agent across Workspace apps
2026-05-19-gemini-spark.whatChanged: Google announced Gemini Spark, a persistent personal agent that acts across Workspace applications under user direction.
2026-05-19-gemini-spark.whyCare: AI at work is moving from a chat tool next to the work to an agent inside the software people already use.
2026-05-19-gemini-spark.before: AI helped in single prompts or inside one application at a time.
2026-05-19-gemini-spark.after: A persistent agent can coordinate work across several everyday applications.
2026-05-19-gemini-spark.learn: Define what users may delegate, which actions need approval and what context the agent may see.
2026-05-19-gemini-spark.architectureImplication: Design for delegation, approvals, context boundaries and user control when agents act across applications.

2026-06-09-fable5.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5, built for long and complex tasks
2026-06-09-fable5.whatChanged: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5. Anthropic says its lead over its other models grows with the length and complexity of the task, across coding, knowledge work, vision and research.
2026-06-09-fable5.whyCare: How long and complex a task a model can finish is becoming a main way to compare models.
2026-06-09-fable5.before: Hard tasks had to be split into many small steps with a person checking each one.
2026-06-09-fable5.after: Stronger models can carry larger projects further before handing control back.
2026-06-09-fable5.learn: Test models on how long and how complex a task they finish reliably. Use your own tasks.
2026-06-09-fable5.architectureImplication: Evaluate models on task length and complexity as well as benchmark scores.

2026-07-20-long-horizon-safety.title: OpenAI moves safety evaluation from single actions to whole trajectories
2026-07-20-long-horizon-safety.whatChanged: OpenAI reported new failure types during limited internal use of a long-running model. It responded with new evaluations, long-horizon alignment work, trajectory monitoring and more user control.
2026-07-20-long-horizon-safety.whyCare: Once systems act over long periods, checking single outputs misses what the sequence of actions is working toward.
2026-07-20-long-horizon-safety.before: Safety checks focused on single responses or short, bounded tasks.
2026-07-20-long-horizon-safety.after: Production controls need to judge sequences of actions and step in during a run.
2026-07-20-long-horizon-safety.learn: Add trajectory monitoring, long-horizon evaluations, approval points and recovery steps to agent designs.
2026-07-20-long-horizon-safety.architectureImplication: Monitor whole agent runs. Define where a run must stop for approval and how to recover it.

2026-09-03-gpt6-astra.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra with gains in computer use, science and cyber
2026-09-03-gpt6-astra.whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra and reported state-of-the-art results on benchmarks for computer use, science, cybersecurity and professional work.
2026-09-03-gpt6-astra.whyCare: Frontier models now operate software and carry out complex professional tasks as well as answering questions.
2026-09-03-gpt6-astra.before: Models were less reliable at long, tool-using professional work and computer use.
2026-09-03-gpt6-astra.after: A frontier model handles a wider set of complex tasks and operates software better.
2026-09-03-gpt6-astra.learn: Test it on your own tool-using tasks. Treat vendor benchmark results as claims until you reproduce them.
2026-09-03-gpt6-astra.architectureImplication: Broader capability needs stronger controls, routing, monitoring and risk assessment around the model.

2026-09-10-financial-services.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for financial services with premium market data
2026-09-10-financial-services.whatChanged: OpenAI launched a financial-services edition of ChatGPT. It combines premium market data from partners such as Daloopa and PitchBook with GPT-6 Astra for research, modeling and client materials.
2026-09-10-financial-services.whyCare: AI products are becoming industry-specific, with data rights and workflows built in.
2026-09-10-financial-services.before: Teams combined a general assistant, data subscriptions, templates and controls themselves.
2026-09-10-financial-services.after: A vertical product packages trusted data, domain workflows, output formats and governance together.
2026-09-10-financial-services.learn: When you compare vertical AI products, check data rights, workflow fit and governance as closely as the model.
2026-09-10-financial-services.architectureImplication: Expect more industry products where data rights and workflow design matter as much as the model.

2026-09-16-work-expansion.title: Research finds AI use adds new recurring tasks to people's jobs
2026-09-16-work-expansion.whatChanged: Economic research reported that some AI-assisted tasks outside a worker's usual occupation become recurring parts of their work.
2026-09-16-work-expansion.whyCare: AI may change what jobs include as well as how fast people work.
2026-09-16-work-expansion.before: Teams measured AI adoption as faster work on the same tasks.
2026-09-16-work-expansion.after: Some workers add new recurring tasks because AI lowers the skill or effort needed.
2026-09-16-work-expansion.learn: Measure changes in tasks and roles alongside time saved.
2026-09-16-work-expansion.architectureImplication: Measure workflow change, task expansion and role redesign alongside time savings.

2026-09-22-gpt-6-sol-luna-cost-capabilit.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and Luna as lower-cost model tiers
2026-09-22-gpt-6-sol-luna-cost-capabilit.whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna on 22 September. Per million tokens, Sol costs $2 input and $10 output, and Luna $0.10 input and $0.50 output. OpenAI says they bring GPT-6 Astra advances to cheaper tiers.
2026-09-22-gpt-6-sol-luna-cost-capabilit.whyCare: More reasoning, coding and agent subtasks may become affordable at high volume. Compare task success, latency and total cost with retries included.
2026-09-22-gpt-6-sol-luna-cost-capabilit.before: Teams kept strong models for hard steps and used older, cheaper models for high-volume steps.
2026-09-22-gpt-6-sol-luna-cost-capabilit.after: Teams can test newer, cheaper tiers for both hard and high-volume steps.
2026-09-22-gpt-6-sol-luna-cost-capabilit.learn: Build task-specific evaluations. Route by accuracy, latency, cache hit rate, retries and cost per successful task.
2026-09-22-gpt-6-sol-luna-cost-capabilit.architectureImplication: Benchmark several models and route by workload and risk. Keep a provider abstraction and a fallback.

2026-10-09-postman-agent-mode-production.title: Postman shows how it limits tools and context for its production agent
2026-10-09-postman-agent-mode-production.whatChanged: Postman and AWS described Agent Mode's design. A root agent narrows over 170 tools to about 15 per task. Schema-aware queries replace many read tools, and context handlers supply relevant state. State-changing actions still need approval. Tool-selection errors rose above about 40 visible tools in Postman's testing.
2026-10-09-postman-agent-mode-production.whyCare: Past a point, more tools and prompt text make agents less reliable. Shaping context and limiting actions keeps them working.
2026-10-09-postman-agent-mode-production.before: Early versions used many small tools and UI-shaped data, which raised errors and latency.
2026-10-09-postman-agent-mode-production.after: Tools are chosen per task, reads use schema-aware queries, and approvals gate changes.
2026-10-09-postman-agent-mode-production.learn: Count your tool catalog as part of the context budget. Select tools per task and keep approval for important writes.
2026-10-09-postman-agent-mode-production.architectureImplication: Give each task a small, relevant tool set and curated context. Keep write approvals, data retention and inference region explicit.

2026-10-09-ai2-gpu-time-budget-scheduler.title: Ai2 replaces GPU priorities with time budgets and preemption contracts
2026-10-09-ai2-gpu-time-budget-scheduler.whatChanged: Ai2 replaced its priority-based GPU scheduler with fair-share allocation weighted by GPU-time budgets, plus minimum-runtime contracts that let resumable jobs be preempted. In 30 days it delivered 98% of allocated GPU hours at 98% occupancy. Debug-job p90 waits fell from two hours to 30 seconds.
2026-10-09-ai2-gpu-time-budget-scheduler.whyCare: Scarce GPUs tempt teams to hold capacity and inflate priorities. Budgets align use with company priorities and let idle capacity be borrowed.
2026-10-09-ai2-gpu-time-budget-scheduler.before: Non-preemptible jobs could hold capacity, priorities inflated, and fixed team allocations left GPUs idle.
2026-10-09-ai2-gpu-time-budget-scheduler.after: GPU time is shared across projects by budget, and resumable work can be preempted after a guaranteed run time.
2026-10-09-ai2-gpu-time-budget-scheduler.learn: Budget GPU time per team. Pair fair share with checkpointing, preemption rules and visible usage data.
2026-10-09-ai2-gpu-time-budget-scheduler.architectureImplication: Shared GPU fleets can use budget-weighted fair share with preemption. Test checkpointing and fragmentation before rollout.

2026-10-07-claude-haiku-55-copilot.title: GitHub brings Claude Haiku 5.5 to all Copilot plans and surfaces
2026-10-07-claude-haiku-55-copilot.whatChanged: GitHub made Claude Haiku 5.5 generally available in Copilot for individual, Business and Enterprise plans, across IDEs, Copilot CLI, cloud agent and github.com. GitHub positions it for fast, high-volume work such as subagents and quick edits. Usage is billed at provider list price.
2026-10-07-claude-haiku-55-copilot.whyCare: Teams get a small, fast model for high-volume subtasks inside their existing coding tools.
2026-10-07-claude-haiku-55-copilot.before: Teams had fewer integrated options for a fast model for subagents and routine coding steps.
2026-10-07-claude-haiku-55-copilot.after: Organizations can enable Haiku 5.5 across Copilot under their model policies.
2026-10-07-claude-haiku-55-copilot.learn: Test it on your coding and subagent tasks. Compare success rate, latency, retries and cost per finished task.
2026-10-07-claude-haiku-55-copilot.architectureImplication: Add Haiku 5.5 as a routing option for short, high-volume tasks. Measure cost per successful task.

2026-10-08-google-gemini-work-agent.title: Google announces a Gemini agent with its own identity for workplace tasks
2026-10-08-google-gemini-work-agent.whatChanged: At Gemini at Work 2026, Google announced a Gemini agent that works across Workspace and connected systems. Team agents get their own accounts and identities, and their access follows existing sharing permissions. Google also described audit trails, sandboxed execution, model routing and spend caps.
2026-10-08-google-gemini-work-agent.whyCare: Agent identity, permissions, audit and cost limits now come packaged in a workplace suite.
2026-10-08-google-gemini-work-agent.before: Enterprises combined chat assistants with separate automations, and handled identity, audit and cost controls in different services.
2026-10-08-google-gemini-work-agent.after: Team agents have their own identities, inherit access from shared resources and run under central controls.
2026-10-08-google-gemini-work-agent.learn: Test agent-owned identity and user-delegated access on one bounded workflow. Check audit trails and spend limits.
2026-10-08-google-gemini-work-agent.architectureImplication: Compare suite-native agents with custom agent stacks on identity, permissions, audit and lock-in. Check availability first.

2026-10-09-copilot-local-sandbox-ga.title: GitHub makes local sandboxing generally available for Copilot coding agents
2026-10-09-copilot-local-sandbox-ga.whatChanged: GitHub made local sandboxing generally available at no extra cost in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and VS Code Agent Host sessions. It limits agent commands' access to files, networks and credentials. Enterprise settings can require it.
2026-10-09-copilot-local-sandbox-ga.whyCare: Coding agents run commands with the developer's privileges. A built-in sandbox makes limiting that access simpler.
2026-10-09-copilot-local-sandbox-ga.before: Copilot CLI commands ran with the user's full access unless teams added other controls.
2026-10-09-copilot-local-sandbox-ga.after: Organizations can turn on OS-level sandboxing across several Copilot surfaces and enforce it centrally.
2026-10-09-copilot-local-sandbox-ga.learn: Test the sandbox's file, network and credential limits on each operating system. Use cloud sandboxes where you need stronger isolation.
2026-10-09-copilot-local-sandbox-ga.architectureImplication: Compare local sandboxing with containers, VMs and GitHub's cloud sandbox. Match the isolation level to your threat model.

2026-10-10-copilot-jetbrains-agent-contr.title: GitHub adds managed model defaults and MCP startup controls to Copilot for JetBrains
2026-10-10-copilot-jetbrains-agent-contr.whatChanged: GitHub added enterprise settings to choose the default Copilot agent model for new JetBrains conversations. Users can still pick another model. A new setting can stop configured MCP servers from starting automatically.
2026-10-10-copilot-jetbrains-agent-contr.whyCare: Administrators get a consistent starting model, and developers control when tools become active. Neither setting restricts which models or MCP tools are allowed.
2026-10-10-copilot-jetbrains-agent-contr.before: JetBrains users chose models with no managed default, and MCP servers started automatically.
2026-10-10-copilot-jetbrains-agent-contr.after: Administrators set the default model, and users can turn off automatic MCP startup.
2026-10-10-copilot-jetbrains-agent-contr.learn: Use model allowlists or a gateway where you must restrict models. Keep MCP permissions and least privilege separate from startup settings.
2026-10-10-copilot-jetbrains-agent-contr.architectureImplication: Treat the default model as a preference. Enforce model policy and MCP permissions through separate controls.

2026-10-12-copilot-telemetry-controls.title: GitHub adds identity attribution and per-category telemetry controls to Copilot
2026-10-12-copilot-telemetry-controls.whatChanged: GitHub added an opt-in setting that records the Copilot account, OS account and host name in OpenTelemetry data. Enterprise settings separately control capture of prompts, responses, tool arguments, tool output and policy details. All capture is off by default.
2026-10-12-copilot-telemetry-controls.whyCare: Enterprises can link agent activity to users and devices without collecting conversation content.
2026-10-12-copilot-telemetry-controls.before: Telemetry used a pseudonymous user ID, and one setting controlled all content capture.
2026-10-12-copilot-telemetry-controls.after: Administrators control identity capture and five content types separately, all off by default.
2026-10-12-copilot-telemetry-controls.learn: Collect the minimum data you need. Content capture can include source code, tool data and local paths.
2026-10-12-copilot-telemetry-controls.architectureImplication: Keep identity and content telemetry as separate policy decisions, set centrally.

2026-10-12-lambda-web-functions.title: AWS launches Lambda Web Functions for HTTP servers and streaming AI endpoints
2026-10-12-lambda-web-functions.whatChanged: AWS introduced Lambda Web Functions, which run standard Node.js HTTP servers, including streaming inference endpoints. One warm environment serves up to 128 concurrent requests. Compute is billed on active CPU time and memory for the environment's lifetime. It launches on Node.js 24, Arm64 and five Regions.
2026-10-12-lambda-web-functions.whyCare: Teams can deploy an HTTP server without rewriting it as an event handler, and pay less for CPU while waiting on I/O.
2026-10-12-lambda-web-functions.before: Lambda required an event-handler model, so HTTP apps needed adapters or separate hosting.
2026-10-12-lambda-web-functions.after: A Node.js HTTP server runs on Lambda with concurrency, native streaming and active-CPU billing.
2026-10-12-lambda-web-functions.learn: Compare it with event-driven functions and containers on concurrency, memory cost, runtime and Region limits.
2026-10-12-lambda-web-functions.architectureImplication: Consider HTTP-native serverless hosting for streaming inference APIs with long I/O waits.

2026-10-14-github-hydrafusion.title: GitHub Copilot HydraFusion drafts and reviews with several models per task
2026-10-14-github-hydrafusion.whatChanged: GitHub updated HydraFusion, its research-preview Copilot orchestrator. Cascade judges a draft and asks a stronger model for a repair only when needed. Critique runs models in parallel to inspect the work. Each model call is billed at its standard rate.
2026-10-14-github-hydrafusion.whyCare: Teams get draft-and-review patterns without building their own harness, though multi-pass work costs more credits and time.
2026-10-14-github-hydrafusion.before: Teams picked one model, or built escalation and review workflows into their own agent harness.
2026-10-14-github-hydrafusion.after: Copilot can pick one model, a judged cascade or parallel critique for each task.
2026-10-14-github-hydrafusion.learn: Compare it with single-model use on real coding tasks. Track accepted changes, regressions, latency and credits. Keep it out of critical workflows while in preview.
2026-10-14-github-hydrafusion.architectureImplication: Choose orchestration per workload based on quality and cost. The preview has no SLA.

2026-10-15-sagemaker-muse-spark-open.title: AWS adds Meta Muse Spark Open to SageMaker JumpStart for in-account deployment
2026-10-15-sagemaker-muse-spark-open.whatChanged: AWS made Meta's Muse Spark Open available in SageMaker JumpStart in BF16 and NVFP4 variants. The 816B-parameter model has 42B active parameters, a 1M-token context window and text, image, document, audio and video input. It launches in two US East Regions.
2026-10-15-sagemaker-muse-spark-open.whyCare: Teams can test a large open-weight model on private code and media without sending data to a third-party API.
2026-10-15-sagemaker-muse-spark-open.before: Teams needed another deployment route to run Muse Spark Open on AWS.
2026-10-15-sagemaker-muse-spark-open.after: Teams can deploy it as a SageMaker endpoint in their own account with VPC, KMS encryption and network isolation.
2026-10-15-sagemaker-muse-spark-open.learn: Benchmark both variants on your tasks. Check the license, quotas and cost, since the endpoint bills on large GPU instances while active.
2026-10-15-sagemaker-muse-spark-open.architectureImplication: Weigh open-weight control against hosted APIs. Size for the full model memory and enforce license, network and cost controls.

2026-10-15-github-copilot-model-deprecat.title: GitHub retires three Copilot models on 16 November 2026
2026-10-15-github-copilot-model-deprecat.whatChanged: GitHub will deprecate Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra across Copilot on 16 November 2026. It recommends Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Luna as replacements, enabled automatically under default model policies.
2026-10-15-github-copilot-model-deprecat.whyCare: Teams using these models have a fixed migration deadline and need to test the replacements first.
2026-10-15-github-copilot-model-deprecat.before: The three models were available across supported Copilot experiences.
2026-10-15-github-copilot-model-deprecat.after: They disappear from most Copilot experiences after 16 November. Opus 4.8 stays for annual individual plans.
2026-10-15-github-copilot-model-deprecat.learn: List where you use these models. Test the replacements on real tasks and check your model policies before the deadline.
2026-10-15-github-copilot-model-deprecat.architectureImplication: Treat hosted models as versioned dependencies. Keep evaluations and a migration path ready for retirements.

2026-10-16-github-open-source-license-co.title: GitHub enforces license policy on new dependencies, including those added by agents
2026-10-16-github-open-source-license-co.whatChanged: GitHub made open source license compliance generally available for Enterprise Cloud with Code Security. Rulesets can block merges until new dependencies meet license policy. A new API lets coding agents check a package before they add it.
2026-10-16-github-open-source-license-co.whyCare: Coding agents add dependencies quickly, so license checks need to happen when they choose a package and again at merge.
2026-10-16-github-open-source-license-co.before: Pull request checks existed, but agents had no generally available API to check a package against policy.
2026-10-16-github-open-source-license-co.after: Agents can check packages through the API, and rulesets enforce policy before merge.
2026-10-16-github-open-source-license-co.learn: Connect your coding agents to the package check. Keep the required merge check as the final gate.
2026-10-16-github-open-source-license-co.architectureImplication: Check license policy at package selection and enforce it again at merge. Audit exceptions.

2026-10-16-reflection-beam-open-model-aw.title: Reflection releases Beam, an open coding model you can run on AWS
2026-10-16-reflection-beam-open-model-aw.whatChanged: Reflection released Beam 1.0, an open-weight coding model with 501B total and 23B active parameters and a reported 1M-token context, under Apache 2.0. AWS offers it through SageMaker JumpStart and HyperPod in two US East Regions.
2026-10-16-reflection-beam-open-model-aw.whyCare: You can now run a coding model for agents inside your own AWS account, under a license that allows commercial use.
2026-10-16-reflection-beam-open-model-aw.before: Teams had to assemble serving for other open coding models themselves, and Beam was not yet available.
2026-10-16-reflection-beam-open-model-aw.after: Teams can deploy Beam through SageMaker JumpStart or HyperPod, or run the weights themselves.
2026-10-16-reflection-beam-open-model-aw.learn: Test Beam on your own agent tasks before you trust its benchmarks. Plan memory for all 501B parameters. Check which regions offer it.
2026-10-16-reflection-beam-open-model-aw.architectureImplication: Compare self-hosting Beam with hosted coding models on quality, serving footprint and cost.

2023-08-02-owasp-llm-top-10.whatChanged: OWASP published version 1.0 of its Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications. It lists the main risks, such as prompt injection and insecure output handling.

2024-08-01-eu-ai-act-in-force.title: EU AI Act enters into force

2025-08-02-eu-ai-act-gpai-obligations.architectureImplication: Use vendor documentation when you select a model and keep it in your risk records.
